exact_predecessor_frontier: Test crash consistency of evidence-epoch renewal as a single state transition by splitting epoch number, epoch_started_at, effect identity fence, and last-certificate pointer across write boundaries; compare non-atomic multi-field renewal against a single versioned renewal record and reject reconstruction that can accept without a self-consistent renewal record.
planned_atomic_boundary: One symbolic crash-injection probe only; no public-source leaf and no second optional effect chain.

probe_model.acceptance_rule: A certificate is actionable only if certificate.epoch == record.epoch AND certificate.effect_id == record.effect_id AND certificate.observed_at >= record.epoch_started_at.

control_result: If certificate acquisition is forbidden whenever the renewal record is not self-consistent, split-field persistence is safety-preserving but introduces fail-closed availability gaps. The unsafe case appears when restart logic treats a partially renewed field set as current authority and permits reacquisition: crash points 1 and 2 can mint a certificate that passes the local epoch/effect/freshness conjunction while being bound to a mixed old/new authority state.
versioned_record_result: A single versioned renewal record containing generation, epoch, epoch_started_at, effect_id, cert_ptr=null and an integrity tag/pointer removes the mixed-authority minting window when replaced atomically. After crash, reconstruction observes either the old coherent generation or the new coherent generation; no certificate may be minted from an intermediate field set. If whole-record atomic replacement is not guaranteed by the transport, use two immutable generations plus one atomic current-generation pointer and fail closed on checksum/version mismatch.
mechanism_revision: Evidence renewal is an authority transition, not a collection of independently current fields. Certificate acquisition must be gated on a self-consistent renewal-generation record. Do not allow reacquisition against a torn generation even when the certificate-level epoch/effect/freshness conjunction would pass.
neuroscience_transfer: Context renewal should behave like latent-state remapping with a commit boundary: new sensory evidence must bind to one coherent context state, not a hybrid of the previous and next context. The relevant safety property is conjunctive binding to a committed latent context, not merely recency tagging.
scope_guard: Tested only a serialized single-writer symbolic renewal with deterministic effect ids, immutable certificate epoch/effect/observation time, one restart after each of four field writes, and optional certificate reacquisition after restart. No claim for concurrent writers, Byzantine/corrupt storage, nondeterministic effect ids, or transports lacking any atomic pointer/replace primitive.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local persistence/readback only; no hosted compute or repository API volume used as computation
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: A renewal generation must be self-consistent before it can authorize certificate acquisition; atomic whole-record replacement or immutable-generation-plus-atomic-pointer satisfies the tested crash model.
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: Pointer publication itself can be acknowledged ambiguously: if the client loses the response after the atomic generation pointer was committed, restart must distinguish committed-new-pointer from uncommitted-old-pointer without duplicating renewal or minting against the wrong generation.

exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: test ambiguous acknowledgement of the atomic renewal-generation pointer. Model a client that writes immutable generation G+1 then attempts one pointer CAS old->G+1, loses the response, and restarts with only durable role-local state. Compare blind retry, read-before-retry, and idempotent pointer target semantics; falsify any route that can create a second renewal generation, regress the pointer, or authorize certificate acquisition before the committed generation is identified.
